title: Noetherian models of a smooth affine group with a connected smooth subgroup
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $G\to S$ be a smooth affine group scheme of finite presentation [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A group scheme is a group object in schemes over its base, with the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme]. Let $H\hookrightarrow G$ be a finitely presented closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion], smooth over $S$, with nonempty geometrically connected fibers [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometric connectedness means connectedness after extending a residue field to an algebraic closure. There exist a subring $A_0\subseteq A$ generated by finitely many elements over $\mathbf Z$, a smooth affine group scheme $G_0$ of finite presentation over $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, and a finitely presented closed subgroup $H_0\hookrightarrow G_0$, smooth with nonempty geometrically connected fibers over $S_0$, together with group-scheme isomorphisms $G_0\times_{S_0}S\simeq G$ and $H_0\times_{S_0}S\simeq H$ compatible with the closed inclusions [def-pc-fibre-product]. The ring $A_0$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $G_0$ is a Noetherian scheme, meaning quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. The isomorphisms preserve multiplication, identity and inverse.

source.place: Conrad, proof of Proposition 2.1.2, printed p.57, descent of affine group and closed subgroup data to finitely generated integer subalgebras, and proof of Proposition 2.1.6, p.62, noetherian reduction preserving smoothness and geometrically connected fibers, citing EGA IV, 8.3.3, 9.7.9 and 17.8.7. This is the simultaneous model assertion, not representability of a normalizer. Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this exact assertion.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The affine description of a closed immersion gives $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$ for a quotient $u:B\twoheadrightarrow C$. Since both structure morphisms are smooth, the affine smoothness criterion gives finite presentations $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(f_1,\ldots,f_s)$ and $C=A[y_1,\ldots,y_t]/(g_1,\ldots,g_v)$. Let $I$ be the directed set of finitely generated integer subrings $A_i\subseteq A$; its ring colimit is $A$. A single $A_i$ contains the coefficients of all the $f_a,g_b$. Define $B_i,C_i$ by these same presentations over $A_i$. Tensoring their presentations with $A$ gives precisely $B,C$. Put $G_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, $H_i=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$. The affine fibre-product formula identifies their base changes with $G,H$, using the specified presentation isomorphisms. The spectra $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ have affine transitions and scheme limit $S$. The presentations give locally finite presentation on the full affine charts; these structure maps are affine by the fibre-product formula and thus quasi-compact and separated by affine-morphism permanence, so they are of finite presentation.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, proof of (1); affine smoothness and tensor interpretation as in Tags 01V6, 01JQ

proof.text: Over the presentations from step 1, the inclusion and the three operations on each group are seven specified affine morphisms: $H\to G$, $G\times_SG\to G$, $S\to G$, $G\to G$, and the corresponding three maps for $H$. Contravariantly these are algebra maps among $A,B,C,B\otimes_AB,C\otimes_AC$. The analogous stage algebras, including triple tensor powers when needed, are finitely presented: base change and composition preserve finite presentation. The affine fibre-product formula identifies all these stage and limit products with the required schemes. Apply the arrow clause (2) of the algebra Hom-descent node to each of the seven maps. Directedness gives a common stage for all seven. Denote the resulting scheme maps by $j_i,m_{G,i},e_{G,i},v_{G,i},m_{H,i},e_{H,i},v_{H,i}$. Their pullbacks, under the fixed isomorphisms of step 1, are exactly the original maps.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, (2); Tag 05G5 and Tag 00F4 for finite presentation of tensor powers

proof.text: For each $Q=G_i,H_i$, form the two sides of the following five equations using its descended maps and the canonical product identifications: $m(m\times1)=m(1\times m)$ on $Q^3$; $m(e\times1)=1_Q$ and $m(1\times e)=1_Q$ on $Q$; $m(v,1)=e\circ p_Q$ and $m(1,v)=e\circ p_Q$ on $Q$, where the last two maps into $Q^2$ use its diagonal. Also form $j_i m_H=m_G(j_i\times j_i)$, $j_i e_H=e_G$, and $j_i v_H=v_Gj_i$. All thirteen pairs become equal over $A$, since they are the original group axioms and subgroup compatibilities. In coordinate rings each pair has finitely presented source and target by step 2. Apply clause (3) of algebra Hom descent to each pair, then take one upper bound of the thirteen stages. The equations now hold at that stage. Thus both models are group objects and $j_i$ respects all operations. Each later base change preserves these equations by functoriality and the universal property of fibre products. This argument does not assume that $A$ is faithfully flat over $A_i$.

source.place: Tag 05N9, lemma-colimit-category-fp-algebras, (3), applied to the explicitly listed finite set of equations

proof.text: The stage morphism $j_i:H_i\to G_i$ is locally of finite type: the finite set of algebra generators of $C_i$ over $A_i$ also generates it over $B_i$ through the descended map. Both schemes and $S_i$ are affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Its limit base change is the given closed immersion $H\hookrightarrow G$. Apply closed-immersion descent to obtain a later stage where $j_i$ is a closed immersion. Work over the cofinal tail beginning at that stage. Closedness persists under further scalar extension: on rings the quotient $B_i\twoheadrightarrow C_i$ tensors to a surjection, since each tensor is a sum of pure tensors and every element of $C_i$ lifts to $B_i$. The affine description of closed immersions gives the assertion at every later stage.

source.place: Tag 01ZP, lemma-descend-closed-immersion-finite-presentation; persistence follows directly from the affine quotient description

proof.text: Every $A_i$ is a finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra, so the Noetherian finite-type-algebra theorem applies, since every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ is principal. Thus $A_i$ is Noetherian; applying the same theorem to $A_i\to B_i$ and $A_i\to C_i$ makes both coordinate rings Noetherian. The finite-type-over-Noetherian-scheme theorem, starting with $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, makes $S_i,G_i,H_i$ Noetherian schemes. Finally $C_i$ is finite type over $B_i$ by the same generators used in step 4. The finite-type-over-Noetherian-ring finite-presentation theorem therefore makes $B_i\to C_i$ finitely presented. Consequently $j_i$ is a finitely presented closed immersion. The assertions hold at every subsequent stage as well, since its base ring remains a finitely generated integer subring and its two coordinate algebras retain finite presentations.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation; scheme consequence Tag 01T6

proof.text: Apply eventual smoothness to each of $G_i\to S_i$ and $H_i\to S_i$. Its hypotheses hold: the stages and both model schemes are affine and therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the two morphisms have finite presentations, and their pullbacks to $S$ are the given smooth structure maps. Take a common upper bound of the two eventual-smoothness stages. Both structure maps are smooth at every subsequent stage, as explicitly supplied by the cited statement. The operations and the closed inclusion remain the base changes of those already constructed.

At this smooth stage let $f_i:H_i\to S_i$ and let $E=\{s\in S_i:n_{f_i}(s)=1\}$, where $n_{f_i}$ counts geometric connected components and assigns count zero to the empty fibre. Since $f_i$ is finitely presented and $S_i$ is Noetherian, the geometric-component-locus theorem says that $E$ is constructible. For any $s\in S$, component-count base change gives $n_{H/S}(s)=n_{f_i}(s_i)$. The left side is one by the nonempty geometrically connected fibre hypothesis. Thus the image of $S$ in $S_i$ lies in $E$. Apply constructible-image descent to the affine-transition system $S_j$ on this tail. It gives $j\geq i$ such that the image of every $S_k$, $k\geq j$, in $S_i$ lies in $E$. For any $t\in S_j$, base change again gives $n_{H_j/S_j}(t)=n_{f_i}(t_i)=1$. A space with exactly one maximal nonempty connected component is nonempty and connected: every point belongs to a connected component, so the unique component is the whole space. Hence all the geometric fibres of $H_j\to S_j$ are nonempty and connected. This treats count zero separately, rather than mistaking empty fibres for connected ones.

Take $A_0=A_j$, $S_0=S_j$, $G_0=G_j$ and $H_0=H_j$. Steps 3--6 give the group objects, finitely presented closed subgroup, smoothness, and Noetherian assertions. Step 7 gives the required geometric fibres. Throughout, the presentation isomorphisms of step 1 identify each descended operation with its original after extension to $A$, and identify $j_j$ with $H\hookrightarrow G$. Therefore those very isomorphisms are group-scheme isomorphisms preserving multiplication, identity, inverse and the closed inclusions, which proves every clause.
